title: Run an Event Quest™
intro: Plan any event, a conference, workshop, fundraiser, festival, market, show or party, through The IV Phases™: what it is for, who owns what, how the day runs, and what lasts after it.

nodes.section: Phase I — What the event is for
nodes.prompt: What is this event for, and what should people feel, learn or remember when it ends?

nodes.section: Phase I — What the event is for
nodes.prompt: Who is the event for first, and who else does it serve: speakers or artists, the team, the venue, sponsors and the community around it?

nodes.section: Phase I — What the event is for
nodes.prompt: What are your non-negotiables: the standards you will not trade away for money or attendance?

Who owns each part: program and content, venue and setup, sound, screens and lighting, power and technical, security and crowd safety, welfare and first aid, registration or ticketing and the door, food and vendors, volunteers and staff? Name one owner for each.
Which permits, licenses, insurance and venue agreements does the event need, and who holds them? (Check the rules where you are.)
What does the event cost, what comes in, and what is your break-even?
How do people arrive and move: registration or ticketing, the door, your capacity limit, crowd flow, accessibility, and entry and exit routes?
What is the run-of-show: doors, each segment or set, changeovers and the finish, and who calls each cue?
What is your technical plan: sound, screens or lighting, power and backup, a test run before doors, and any volume limits?

What is your safety and welfare plan: first aid, water and food, heat or cold, accessibility, a quiet space, emergencies, alcohol or other substances as the law and venue require, and how a problem is reported and who acts?
How will your team communicate on the day, who makes which decisions, and what happens when the plan breaks?
What will you record afterward: attendance, what worked, what did not, incidents and lessons?
How will you thank and keep the speakers or artists, team, venue, sponsors and community, and what do you owe them after the event?
What will you write down so someone else could run the next one: contacts, contracts, run sheets and setup plans?
What would make this event part of something lasting: a series, a collective, a name someone else could carry on?
